scope: retrospective attrition-classification configuration, input and outcome contracts, leakage-safe model selection, rejected-model isolation, exact scoring features, finite probabilities, stale-state clearing, aggregate-only product boundaries, diagnostic explanation integrity, and cross-product compatibility
confirmed_findings_fixed: Invalid, reversed, boolean or non-finite predictive configuration could reach scoring and categorization paths; thresholds, split ratio, seed and explanation sample size now fail closed at initialization.

Legacy feature-matrix training could accept single-class, under-supported, misaligned, non-numeric or non-finite inputs; the retained compatibility path now enforces binary outcomes, minimum support, aligned indices and a finite numeric feature contract.
Failed or rejected training could leave a previously fitted model available; training clears model, feature and explanation state before work and again on failure.
Candidate selection now respects configured model families and rejects unavailable or non-finite candidates rather than silently substituting an unreviewed path.
Scoring now requires the exact trained feature names and order, a finite matrix, an identified positive class and finite probabilities in the unit interval.
A retrospectively fitted model that fails release reliability gates is no longer left trained for direct scoring.
The legacy employee-level prediction list and rule-based employee action recommendations are disabled at the engine boundary; governed product use remains aggregate-only.
Feature-importance and SHAP diagnostic outputs now fail closed when class, dimensionality or finite-value contracts do not reconcile.
interpretation_boundary: MLEngine is a retrospectively evaluated classifier component. Its scores are not validated future-departure probabilities, individual employment decisions, causal explanations or recommended actions. Product exposure remains governed and aggregate-only until a model passes the separate release and activation controls.
remaining_scientific_limits: The IBM synthetic holdout does not establish transportability, calibration or prospective accuracy for an organization or future time period.
Temporal and entity-separated validation, subgroup stability, drift monitoring, calibration intervals and mature-outcome follow-up remain required before stronger predictive claims.
SHAP availability and mathematical consistency do not establish causal explanation, intervention value or fairness.
The low-level preprocessed-matrix training method cannot attest upstream preprocessing isolation and remains an explicitly unvalidated compatibility surface.
No employee-level prediction list or automated employment-action recommendation is within the validated product scope.
release_gate: Local forensic and cross-product validation is clean. Remote CI rerun, independent review and explicit owner authorization remain pending.
